q: Starfish, also called sea stars, belong to which group of animals?
explain: Despite the name, starfish aren't fish at all. They're echinoderms, cousins of sea urchins and sand dollars, which is why scientists prefer the name sea star.
searchNote: NOAA says starfish are not fish but echinoderms, related to sea urchins and sand dollars, and are also called sea stars.

q: What do sea stars use instead of blood to carry nutrients around their bodies?
explain: Sea stars have no blood. They pump seawater through a network of canals called the water vascular system, which also powers their tube feet.

source2.title: Bat star

searchNote: NOAA states sea water, instead of blood, is used to pump nutrients through their bodies via a water vascular system. MBA profiles also mention a water vascular system instead of a traditional circulatory system.

choices: They shed the tip of each foot
They wait for the glue to dry

q: Roughly how fast can a sunflower sea star move across the seafloor?

q: About how many tube feet does an adult sunflower sea star move on?
explain: An adult sunflower sea star glides on roughly 15,000 tube feet, which is how it manages such a brisk pace for a sea star.

q: What can a sea star do if a predator damages one of its arms?
choices: Drop the arm and grow a new one
Pull the arm inside its body
Harden the arm into a shell

q: How do many sea stars start digesting a meal like a mussel?
choices: They grind it with hard teeth
They soak it up through their skin
They push their stomach out onto it
explain: Many sea stars push their stomach out of their body and over the prey, digesting it outside before pulling the stomach back in.

q: How does a sea star get into a clam or mussel that is shut tight?
choices: It drills a hole with a rasping tongue
It pulls the shells apart with its tube feet
It cracks the shell against a rock
explain: A sea star suctions its tube feet onto both halves of the shell and slowly pulls them apart.
searchNote: NPS says sea stars use their tube feet to suction onto the shells of bivalves (animals with two shells) and pry them apart.

q: How long can it take an ochre sea star to digest a meal?
explain: Ochre sea stars release enzymes that turn prey tissue to liquid, and the whole digestion process can take two to three days.
searchNote: Aquarium of the Pacific: ochre sea stars release digestive enzymes that liquefy prey tissues; digestion can take two to three days.

q: How many stomachs does an ochre sea star have?
explain: The ochre sea star has two: a cardiac stomach that it pushes out through its mouth onto prey, and an internal pyloric stomach.
searchNote: Aquarium of the Pacific describes a cardiac stomach that extends out through the mouth and an internal pyloric stomach.

q: Where are a bat star's light-sensing eyespots?
choices: At the tip of each arm
In the middle of its upper side
explain: Bat stars have a simple eyespot at the end of each arm. It senses light rather than forming sharp images, and helps the star find its way and its food.

searchNote: Aquarium of the Pacific: bat stars have eye spots at the end of each arm to aid in finding food. MBA also mentions light-detecting eyespots.

q: Why is the bat star called a bat star?
choices: Webbing between its arms looks batlike
It hangs upside down in sea caves
explain: The bat star's short, triangular arms are joined by webbing, giving it the look of a bat's wing. It's a scavenger found from Alaska to Baja California.

q: What does a sunflower sea star do with a sea urchin it catches?
choices: Cracks it open with its arms
Drags it back to a burrow
Swallows it whole, then spits out the shell

searchNote: MBA: a sunflower star can swallow an entire sea urchin, digest it internally and then expel the urchin's test.
